corrections.reason: The word for thirst in Ge'ez/Amharic is ጽምዕ (with 6th-order ዕ), not ጽምፅ. Visually, the glyph at the end of በጽምዕ is ዕ.
Traditional Andemta abbreviation 'በቷ' (በተባለው / በተጠቀሰው) before 'መጣፍ ሰጥተውት'. Visually, the character has the labialized/wa-hook at the bottom of ተ (ቷ).
The printed glyph has the side stroke of 2nd-order ሁ ('ሁነ'), matching the archaic spelling used throughout this column.
In the story of Abba Silvanus, the monk asks 'ተደራሩ አኃው' ('Did the brothers eat dinner / ተደራሩ?'), which is answered on the next line by 'እወ ተደሩ'. Visually, the glyph is ሩ.
The word is 'እንዳንዱ' (like one of them, translating 'ከመ ፩ እምእሉ'). Visually, the right-side stroke of 2nd-order ዱ is present.
